message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to staying up‑to‑date with the latest sports news:

| Source | How it works | Pros | Cons |
|--------|--------------|------|------|
| **Google News** (news.google.com) | Search “sports” or set up a custom feed. | Aggregates many outlets; free; easy to filter by region/time. | Ads; may show duplicate stories from different sites. |
| **ESPN / BBC Sport / Sky Sports** | Visit the site or download their mobile app. | In‑depth coverage, live scores, podcasts. | Some content behind paywalls; heavy ads on free tier. |
| **Reddit** (r/sports, r/nba, r/football, etc.) | Subscribe to subreddits and enable notifications. | Real‑time discussion, insider rumors, community sentiment. | Moderately noisy; quality varies. |
| **Twitter** | Follow official team accounts, leagues, journalists, and hashtags (#NBA, #FIFA). | Instant updates, breaking news, direct quotes. | Information overload; requires filtering. |
| **RSS Feeds** | Use an RSS reader (Feedly, Inoreader) and add feeds from your favorite sites. | Customizable, ad‑free, offline reading. | Requires setup; some sites don’t offer feeds. |
| **News APIs** (e.g., NewsAPI.org, GDELT, Bing News API) | Call the API with query “sports” and optional filters (country, category). | Programmatic access; integrate into dashboards or bots. | Rate limits on free tiers; may need a subscription for high volume. |
| **Push Notification Services** (Pushover, Pushbullet, Telegram Bot) | Set up a bot or service that forwards headlines via push. | Immediate alerts on phone/computer. | Requires initial configuration; may need a small fee for advanced features. |

### Quick Setup Example – Using NewsAPI.org

1. Sign up at https://newsapi.org and grab your API key.  
2. Install `requests` if you haven’t already (`pip install requests`).  
3. Run this simple script to fetch the top 5 sports headlines:

```python
import requests

API_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'
url = ('https://newsapi.org/v2/top-headlines?'
       'category=sport&language=en&pageSize=5&apiKey=' + API_KEY)

response = requests.get(url)
data = response.json()

for article in data['articles']:
    print(f"{article['title']}\n{article['source']['name']} - {article['publishedAt']}\n")
```

Replace `'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'` with your actual key. This will give you a quick snapshot of what’s trending.

### Tips for Filtering Noise

- **Use “filter” or “search” features** on sites/apps to narrow down to specific leagues or teams.  
- **Set up keyword alerts** (Google Alerts, Twitter lists) for names of players or events you care about.  
- **Leverage “read later” services** (Pocket, Instapaper) to save articles for offline reading.  

Pick one or combine several methods depending on how deep you want to dive and whether you prefer passive scrolling or active curation. Happy following!
